DI G AUP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OP'NION NO. 11 FEB 19 2025 ATTY. KENNETH S. NG Counsel for Casetech Inc. 8F Tower Double Dragon Plaza Macapagal Ave., Pasay City Dear Atty. Ng: This has reference to your letter dated 21 November 2024 seeking this Department's legal opinion on whether or not the sale of real property of a closed business is subject to Local Business Tax. Per the representation, Casetech is a corporation that was duly established and exists under the laws of the Republic of the Philippines. You stated that Casetech's 2024 business permit in Quezon City allows it to sell supplies, goods, merchandise, or products of all types, both consumable and non-consumable. You then represented that Casetech decided to close its operations and sell its real properties situated in Quezon City due to business losses incurred by the corporation. However, you alleged that after paying the seventy five percent of one percent (75% of 1%) local transfer tax due on the sale of real property, the local government of Quezon City assessed you with a two percent (2%) Local Business Tax, which was also based on the selling price. Thus, your request for legal opinion. At the onset, please be informed that the sale of real property of a closed business is not subject to Local Business Tax. The Bureau of Local Governance Finance Memorandum Circular No. 001-2020 (January 02, 2020) provides that the sale of real properties or realty assets, unless one is engaged in business of buying or selling real estate, shall not form part of the gross sales or receipts. We are of the considered view that when a business is closed, its activities cease to be considered "business operations." The sale of its real property is treated as a capital transaction, not as part of regular business activities. Considering that the Casetech is closed and is in the process of winding-up, the sale of their real properties shall only be subject to the tax on transfer of real property ownership "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

pursuant to Section 1351 of the Local Government Code in relation to Section 1512 thereof, but it cannot be subject to, or be liable to pay any local business tax for such sale.3 Further, it should be noted that Casetech is not engaged in the sale of real properties, thus, such sale of their real properties should be treated as part of winding-up and as a capital transaction. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA/RPB/LLLS-LRALLD/lasm Copy fumished: KARL CAESAR R. RIMANDO, CESO Ill Regional Director DILG - MIMAROPA Section 135. Tax on Transfer Of Real Property Ownership. (a) The province may impose a tax on the sale , donation, barter, or on any other mode of transferring ownership Or title Of real property at the rate of not rnore than fifty percent (50%) of the one percent (1%) of the total consideration involved in the acquisition of the property or of the fair market value in case the monetary consideration involved in the transfer is not substantial, whichever is higher. The sale, transfer or other disposition of real property pursuant to R.A. NO. 6657 shall be exempt from this tax. (b) For this purpose, the Register of Deeds of the province concerned shall, before registering any deed, require the presentation of the evidence of payment of this tax. The provincial assessor shall likewise make the same requirement before cancelling an old tax declaration and issuing a new one in place thereof, Notaries public shall furnish the provincial treasurer with a copy of any deed transferring ownership or title to any real property within thirty (30) days from the date Of notarization. 2 Section 151. Scope Of Taxing Powers. - Except as otherwise provided in this Code, the city, may levy the taxes, fees, and charges which the province or municipality may impose: Provided, however, That the taxes, fees and charges levied and collected by highly urbanized and independent component cities shall accrue to them and distributed in accordance with the provisions Of this Code. The rates of taxes that the city may lew may exceed the maximum rates allowed for the province or municipality by not more than fifty percent (50%) except the rates of professional and amusement taxes. 3 BLGF Opinion dated 18 August 2014.
